title: Enterprise Core Account Executive, UK
descriptionHtml:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

Are you a high-achieving sales professional ready to digitally transform the physical operations that power our planet? Samsara is seeking a driven Enterprise (Core) Account Executive to introduce our cutting-edge Connected Operations® Platform to Enterprise-sized customers across the UK. This is a unique opportunity to sell a much-needed product into a historically underserved market, working directly with leaders to drive real-world impact and unlock significant career progression. As a Strategic AE you will be helping large mid-market and enterprise sized customers consolidate outdated technologies, digitize workflows, and unlock game-changing data insights that will transform their businesses. We are helping the companies that literally keep our lights on, put food on our tables, and build our communities to become safer, more efficient, and more sustainable. Typical sales will be $100k to $500k, and typically involve POCs, multiple stakeholders, managing trials, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to executives and CXOs.

In this role, you will:

  • Develop Executive-Level relationships within strategic, named accounts
  • Own customer engagements end-to-end, from prospecting and qualification to close
  • Demonstrate excellent solution-based sales process in complex sales campaigns
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years experience in a full-cycle, closing sales role
  • Proven expertise winning new business logos through a repeatable sales motion
  • Demonstrable expertise in strategic outbound prospecting, particularly via inside sales
  • Proven track record of consistent quota over-achievement in Enterprise level accounts, winning multiple $100k+ ARR transactions
  • Experience handling enterprise deal sizes with multiple stakeholders at C-Level
  • Value based selling approach
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability thriving in a dynamic, fast-paced environment
  • Working remotely in UK, however comfortable traveling to meet customers as needed

An ideal candidate also has:

  • SaaS sales experience
  • Experience working with line of business stakeholders (Operations, Finance, IT)
  • Comfortable in a dynamic, customer facing environment
  • MEDDIC experience or similar (Sandler Pain Funnel, etc)
  • Excited about solving new problems in innovative ways
  • Highly collaborative with a growth mindset.
  • Awards for top achievement (President's club, Winner's circle, Top 10%)
  • Passion for the world of operations!

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in ----- ----- or ----- For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

title: Events Lead, UK & International
descriptionHtml:
Substack is building a new economic engine for culture, giving the brightest, most interesting and creative people on the internet the power of their own publishing platform. Substack empowers creators with financial autonomy, ownership and a direct connection to their communities. Substack’s model, based on direct subscriptions, has fueled an explosion of independent publishing and is revolutionizing culture.

 

We're looking for an Events Lead, UK & International to create and execute an exceptional year-round programme of events in the UK in service of our creators and our mission to be a new home of culture, and oversee the delivery of our growing calendar of events internationally too. This means you’ll devise the strategy, planning, and execution of Substack's brand events portfolio in the UK whilst simultaneously building the framework for our growing international activity, from flagship brand moments in London to intimate creator gatherings in Sydney.

 

You’ll create meaningful brand and creator events that are genuinely creative, unique and fun to attend, help foster our community of bestsellers and attract more people to join Substack, and show people they are part of something truly special by being part of our platform. You'll work at the intersection of culture, technology, and media, partnering with some of the most interesting voices shaping our world, across the ideological spectrum.

 

This role reports to the Head of Communications & Brand and is based in London.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Shape the strategy. Develop and execute a UK events strategy that advances Substack's brand and business goals in the UK, and ideate and oversee events in key territories internationally with the Head of International and country leads. Identify innovative opportunities to enhance our brand, drive cultural conversation, and attract new creators and subscribers.

  • Drive execution excellence. Manage the full event lifecycle in the UK—from concept and promotion through on-the-ground coordination —ensuring every detail reflects the quality and creativity of the Substack brand. You will also be responsible for ensuring that your events travel far and wide on social and in the press, as a key pillar of our brand marketing strategy.

  • Enable partnerships. Empower our Partnership Leads to bring market-specific event ideas to life, providing strategic guidance and operational support to ensure strong execution in key territories.

  • Manage resources strategically. Manage a UK events budget with clear goals, measurement frameworks, and ROI tracking, and build effective processes internationally. This includes building methodologies to demonstrate impact and communicate wins internally.

  • Recruit and lead freelancers. Leverage your exceptional network of freelancers and contractors to deliver outstanding results for Substack and support international partnership leads to source the best talent for their markets.

  • Scale thoughtfully. Design events that can be replicated to reach key audiences across strategic territories and regions without losing their impact or authenticity.

  • Collaborate across functions. Partner with internal teams, UK and international agencies, and vendors to deliver high-impact experiences while maintaining fiscal discipline and operational excellence.

 

About You:

  • Significant managerial experience. 8+ years in experiential event marketing and production. You've built and scaled event strategies that delivered measurable business impact.

  • Strategic vision with an operational can-do attitude. You think big picture while obsessing over details. You're an exceptional communicator and organizer who will translate vision into flawless execution.

  • Creative flair. You’re a natural storyteller and ideas person who loves conceiving ideas that are unexpected and brilliant.

  • Industry connections. You have a deep network of premier agencies and vendors across creative, production, and experiential disciplines.

  • Relationship-builder. You cultivate strong cross-functional partnerships and inspire creative problem-solving.

  • Cultural fluency. You're familiar with Substack as a creator or subscriber, and you’re excited to help champion our mission.

  • Entrepreneurial drive. You thrive in startup environments where you're building from scratch.

  • Flexibility to travel. Available to travel globally to oversee on-site execution when needed.

Substack offers a competitive compensation package that includes salary, equity, and exceptional benefits. The salary range for this role is £85,000-£100,000 with final offers based on experience and expertise.

Substack is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or transgender status), age, national origin, veteran or disability status. We’re seeking people passionate about enabling independent expression and building a better business model for creators. If you want to see what media, communities, and content can become when unmoored from advertising models, and you have the skills and experience to contribute, we’d love to meet you.

title: Expert Site Reliability Engineer - Edge Infrastructure (f/m/d)
descriptionHtml:
We see the potential inside everything and everyone. Starting with you.

Orbem uses AI to industrialize MRI, delivering non-invasive insight into everything from fruits to eggs to the human body. We are transforming what is becoming the world's largest biological dataset into actionable intelligence to reduce waste, increase quality, and accelerate the shift toward a more sustainable and healthier future.

Headquartered and founded in Munich, Germany, with an office now in Houston, Texas, our world-class team is scaling inside-out technology to transform how humanity sees and understands biological matter.

Help us see what's possible. Join us.

Your Role

Orbem’s AI-powered MRI systems run on edge infrastructure deployed directly at customer sites, such as hatcheries and food processing plants. As an Expert Site Reliability Engineer, you will own the reliability, availability, and performance of this growing global fleet.

You are the team’s deepest technical authority on the on-premise platform, setting architecture and standards through hands-on expertise. You will own the hardware, network, operating system, and Kubernetes layers that power teams like Data, Machine Learning, and Software.

Your Day-to-Day

As an Individual Contributor on the expert track, your responsibilities center entirely on deep technical ownership and execution:

Edge Infrastructure Ownership

  • Own the reliability and lifecycle of our edge racks: server hardware, network equipment, custom Linux-based OS, and the GPU-enabled Kubernetes layer running our AI classification services.

  • Design and improve automation for provisioning our growing fleet (50+ edge clusters and counting) using tools like Terraform, BMC/IPMI, and router APIs.

  • Maintain the secure network connecting edge deployments to our central cloud, and the tooling that enables safe software delivery to the fleet.

Reliability & Incident Management

  • Lead post-incident reviews and turn findings into lasting, automated fixes.

  • Extend our observability stack (Prometheus, custom hardware exporters, Grafana, Datadog) to catch issues proactively, often before customers notice.

Architecture, Collaboration & Craft

  • Act as the top-level technical escalation point, personally helping resolve the most complex support and production issues.

  • Collaborate with stakeholders (with the eventual support of a Product Manager) to gather requirements and manage technical alignment.

  • Automate away repetitive manual work, applying the same rigor to internal tooling as to a customer-facing product.

Behavioral competencies

title: Field Chief Technology Officer (Field CTO)
descriptionHtml:
MinIO is the data and memory foundation for enterprise AI. Built for the speed, scale, and economics that AI and analytics demand, AIStor and MemKV unify every layer of the data stack, from agentic and inference context memory to tables and objects across core, edge, and cloud. Trusted by 77% of the Fortune 100, MinIO is redefining how AI factories, intelligent applications, and autonomous agents secure, persist, and unlock the full value of their data.

We are seeking a highly technical, visionary, and customer-centric Field CTO to act as our premier technical ambassador. In this role, you will bridge the gap between MinIO’s engineering innovation and the strategic business needs of our largest, most complex enterprise customers.

As a Field CTO, you will engage in peer-to-peer conversations with enterprise C-suites (CIOs, CTOs, CDOs) and lead architectural discussions with principal engineers. A deep, hands-on understanding of modern AI architectures (LLMs, RAG, deep learning pipelines) and modern analytics data systems (Iceberg, Delta Lake, Trino, Spark) is mandatory. You will not only evangelize MinIO’s capabilities but also act as a trusted advisor, helping organizations architect their data infrastructure to support next-generation workloads. 

What You Will Do

  • Executive Advisory & Evangelism: Act as a trusted technical advisor to C-level executives at Fortune 500 companies. Articulate the strategic value of high-performance object storage in the context of AI readiness and data democratization.
  • Architectural Leadership: Design and validate complex, large-scale architectures for enterprise customers. Guide them in integrating MinIO seamlessly into their AI/ML pipelines and modern data lakehouse ecosystems.
  • Industry Thought Leadership: Represent MinIO at major industry conferences, webinars, and meetups. Write technical whitepapers, reference architectures, and blog posts focusing on the intersection of object storage, generative AI, and modern analytics.
  • Pre-Sales & Post-Sales Strategic Support: Partner closely with enterprise sales and customer success teams on high-stakes deals. Unblock technical objections and provide strategic guidance during Proof of Concepts (PoCs) and large-scale deployments.
  • Product Strategy Feedback Loop: Serve as the "voice of the customer" to MinIO’s product and engineering teams. Distill market trends, customer pain points, and emerging AI/Analytics patterns into actionable product requirements.

Your Skills and Experience

  • 10+ years of experience in technical leadership roles (e.g., Enterprise Architect, Chief Architect, VP of Engineering, or previous Field CTO).
  • Demonstrated experience in a customer-facing or evangelist capacity, successfully presenting to both highly technical audiences and C-level business executives.

AI & Machine Learning Architectures:

  • Deep architectural understanding of Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs), including Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflows and vector databases (e.g., Milvus, Qdrant, Pinecone).
  • Strong knowledge of AI/ML data pipelines and frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, Ray, Hugging Face).
  • Understanding of hardware bottlenecks in AI, specifically the challenge of feeding data to GPUs (GPU data starvation) and how high-throughput storage solves this.

Modern Analytics & Data Systems:

  • Expertise in Open Table Formats (Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi, Delta Lake) and their integration with object storage.
  • Proficiency with modern query engines and compute frameworks (Trino, Presto, Apache Spark, Flink, StarRocks).
  • Solid grasp of the evolution from traditional data warehouses to modern Data Lakehouse architectures.

Infrastructure & Cloud-Native Tech:

  • Strong command of Kubernetes, containerization, and cloud-native orchestration.
  • Deep understanding of the AWS S3 API, RESTful APIs, and distributed systems design.

title: Finance
descriptionHtml:
About Nomos

Europe pays more than twice as much for electricity as the US or Asia. To reach competitive price levels, Europe has to lean on solar and deliver the flexibility that makes this feasible. Nomos is building a full-stack power company to unlock that flexibility by connecting millions of homes to Europe’s energy markets.

At Nomos, we care about our craft and take full responsibility for what we build. We hire for spikes, not an absence of weaknesses, and look for exceptional ability backed by a record of achievement. This has brought together IMO and IOI medalists, former founders and Olympic athletes in a team whose individual strengths reinforce one another.

 

What you’ll do

Nomos operates at the intersection of energy and finance. You will build and run our finance function, taking responsibility for the liquidity we need and the capital entrusted to us.

  • Plan and manage liquidity across electricity trading, household payments, and company operations.

  • Define and enforce how money moves: spending, approvals, and financial controls.

  • Run accounting, payroll, and the month-end close, with reliable reporting for the founders and investors.

 

Exciting challenges

  • Build the function from scratch. Decide what we run ourselves, where we need external expertise, and what we can automate. Work with engineering to build processes that stay accurate as transaction volumes grow.

  • Put our capital to work carefully. Understand what we can commit, anticipate future funding needs, and challenge spending that does not justify itself. As Nomos grows, explore where financial products could strengthen our energy offering.

 

Who you are

  • You treat our capital as your own. You’ve run finance before or can show the depth and judgement to build the function. You trace numbers back to their source and challenge the assumptions behind them. Before a new product launches or a partnership grows, you’ve worked through what it means for our finances.

  • You are allergic to loose ends. A number that almost reconciles is a number that is wrong. You find the discrepancy before anyone asks. You’re keen to use automation and AI to make the work more reliable.

  • German and English, both fluent. Accounting, payroll, and tax all happen in German here.

 

References

Anne Roellgen

 

Why join us?

As an early member of Nomos, you’ll help shape the company and share in its financial upside. Backed by Index Ventures, we’re building a European category leader in one of the world’s largest industries, making electricity affordable and Europe more competitive.

Building a power company from scratch brings complex, rewarding challenges and the chance to solve Europe’s energy crisis for the long term. You’ll learn from people with exceptional depth in their fields, challenge each other’s thinking and take responsibility from the start.

title: Finance Operations Associate
descriptionHtml:
View our much better version of this job spec on our careers page: https://juro.notion.site/fao

***

THE KEY BITS

  • Location: We can currently only accept applications from candidates that are located and have long-term working rights in the UK.

  • Flexibility: We have office hubs in London and Boston, as well as no-office hubs in several European countries. We operate a choice-first work approach that lets you work fully remotely from Day One even if you’re near an office hub.

  • Salary: We benchmarked £45,000 + equity at IC2 in our progression framework for someone based in the UK. Let us know in your application if you like the look of the role but the salary doesn’t match what you’re looking for.

  • Interviews: 2 stages totalling around 2.5 hours over 2 weeks, plus some prep for a task.

  • Start date: As soon as you can start.

  • Reporting to: Ryan, Interim Finance Director (while Eimear, Finance Director, is on leave)

  • More info: The FAQ below, juro.com/careers, our handbook or ask ----- style="min-height:1.5em">

    HELP US HELP THE WORLD AGREE FASTER

    Juro has big ambitions: to make it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. And we'll need help doing it.

    Legal tech is on the rise, with Goldman Sachs estimating that 44% of legal tasks can be automated with generative AI. With the brand we have built and the agility of early stage we are well placed to capture this opportunity.

    Juro bills customers and pays suppliers across UK and US entities, and the volume keeps growing. We’re looking for someone who carries the day-to-day weight of finance operations together with the team.

    Roughly 60% of your week goes on AP/AR, and the rest is month-end and reporting support: reconciliations, revenue review, and pulling together what’s needed for statutory accounts, audit requests and VAT returns.

    You won’t be doing this alone: you’ll work closely with Charlotte, our Financial Controller, who owns the close, and Ryan, our Interim Finance Director (stepping in for Eimear), who leads the Finance function.

    Your mission is to:

    Own invoicing, payables and collections end-to-end so Juro gets paid efficiently, accurately and with strong control of cash, and support month-end so leadership can trust the numbers.

    Success looks like:

    1. Invoices done right first time: Contracts are turned into accurate invoices with minimal rework or back-and-forth with Sales and Customer Success.

    2. Money moving smoothly: Customers pay on time and suppliers are paid accurately across our UK and US entities. You keep an up-to-date view of what’s owed in and out, and Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) comes down over time.

    3. Reliable month-end support: Your reconciliations are accurate and on time, you flag escalations early, and you contribute to month-end, revenue review and statutory reporting.

    4. Solid, scalable ops: Processes are well controlled (from supplier onboarding and bank detail checks to payment run approvals), audit-ready, and increasingly automated inside Rillet (our ERP) and Ramp (our spend management system). You improve the process notes rather than just following them.

    We care about building a diverse team where everyone feels they belong. That’s why our perks & benefits and choice-first work approach are designed with inclusivity in mind. Read more in our diversity, inclusion & belonging hub.

    WHO WE LOOK FOR

    Research shows that while men apply to jobs if they meet ~60% of criteria, women and those in traditionally under-represented groups tend to apply only if they check all boxes. So if you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit.

    To succeed here:

    Every Juror finds their balance across our four principles. We hire, develop and celebrate people who live them every day.

    Curious how you’d fit? Try our personality quiz to see how you map against our principles.

    On top of that, you have been part of a journey where:

    • You’ve done both AR and AP: raising invoices, handling billing queries, chasing payments or paying suppliers.

    • You’ve been the #1 point of contact for customers or suppliers on billing and payments. You can be firm about an overdue balance without damaging the relationship, and you keep Sales, CS and budget holders in the loop.

    • You’ve helped with a month-end, e.g. by doing bank or ledger reconciliations.

    • You’ve used finance systems day to day (NetSuite, Rillet, Xero, Ramp or similar) and pick up new tools quickly.

    • You read contracts carefully enough to know what should be invoiced, when, and what’s unclear, and you work with Sales and CS to get it right.

    • You notice repetitive manual work and want to fix it, whether that’s with a better spreadsheet, an automation or AI.

    Bonus points if:

    • You’ve worked with SaaS contracts or subscription billing.

    • You’ve helped with VAT returns, US sales tax, revenue reporting or audit requests.

    • You’ve worked in a multi-entity (UK/US) business with multi-currency invoicing.

    This job likely isn’t for you if:

    • You’re mainly looking for formal accounting training or a pathway to becoming ACA-qualified.

    • You want to own the month-end close or focus on technical accounting, rather than a hands-on mix of finance operations and reporting support.

    • You prefer clearly defined, static processes and don’t enjoy owning messy, real-world problems and making them better (especially with AI).

    OUR MISSION

    Juro exists to help the world agree faster by making it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts.

    The load on legal teams is increasing as business teams move faster with the help of AI. The only way out is to deploy AI within the legal team so that (a) routine contract work can be executed autonomously and (b) lawyers’ time is reserved for problem solving.

    It’s like having an extra team member that is always on and takes on heavy lifting. Just like an in-house lawyer, Juro:

    • is present for, and trusted by, business teams

    • owns contracts from first draft to signature and beyond

    • builds judgement from every contract it works on

    …all within guardrails controlled by the legal team.

    GOT MORE QUESTIONS?

    • Our extended job description for this role: https://juro.notion.site/fao

    • Our company handbook: https://juro.notion.site/handbook

    • Our careers page: https://juro.notion.site

    There, you'll find answers on topics such as career progression, inclusion & belonging, the interview process, benefits and more. Or reach ----- for anything.

title: Financial Control, Accountant
descriptionHtml:
About Us

ClearBank is a technology-enabled bank transforming banking infrastructure through innovative technology and a full banking licence. We provide cloud-based banking and payment solutions to a growing range of clients and are committed to delivering reliable, scalable financial services while maintaining the highest standards of financial control, governance and regulatory compliance.

The Financial Control team is responsible for ensuring ClearBank’s general ledgers are controlled, maintained and reconciled to support timely and accurate reporting across the organisation and externally to regulators and tax authorities. As ClearBank continues to grow, the team plays a critical role in building scalable, efficient and well-controlled finance processes that support the Bank’s strategic ambitions.

Role Purpose

The Financial Control Lead owns allocated month-end activities within a small, hands-on team, supporting accurate, timely and well-controlled financial information.

Reporting to the Financial Control Manager, you will complete month-end tasks, investigate balances and variances, and prepare accounting entries and reconciliations to keep the general ledger accurate and fully supported.

The role will also be expected to stay close to all key aspects of the Financial Control team’s remit, including journals, reconciliations, reporting inputs, controls, audit support, process documentation and stakeholder queries. As ClearBank continues to grow, the Financial Control Lead will be at the forefront of identifying, driving and implementing scalable, efficient and well-controlled processes, helping the team reduce manual effort while maintaining strong financial control standards.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Control & Reporting

  • Own allocated month-end close activities and ensure they are delivered accurately and on time.

  • Prepare, review and approve general ledger journals as required, ensuring postings are technically accurate, appropriately supported and comply with internal control requirements.

  • Own revenue and expense analysis for the relevant areas, ensuring variances are investigated, understood and appropriately communicated to stakeholders.

  • Own the monthly capitalisation and amortisation process for intangible assets, ensuring entries are accurate, supported and appropriately controlled.

  • Partner with Financial Planning & Analysis to ensure accruals and accounting adjustments are identified, calculated and recorded accurately.

  • Prepare, review and approve bank reconciliations as required, ensuring reconciling items are investigated and resolved promptly.

  • Own monthly balance sheet reconciliations for the relevant areas, including preparing and reviewing reconciliations where required, ensuring all balances are fully supported and outstanding issues are appropriately managed.

  • Take ownership of non-automated accounting entries, ensuring they are accurate, appropriately supported, controlled and clearly documented, with clear audit trails maintained.

  • Build and implement scalable, efficient processes while remaining hands-on in day-to-day delivery where needed.

  • Support the preparation of management, regulatory, statutory and tax reporting requirements as required.

  • Ensure compliance with accounting policies, financial reporting standards and internal control frameworks

Systems, Automation & Continuous Improvement

  • Help drive and implement automation and process improvements across finance processes, controls and reporting activities, helping to reduce manual effort and improve scalability.

  • Lead initiatives to automate the capture and posting of accounting entries from ClearBank’s core banking and operational systems into the general ledger.

  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability and data quality across Financial Control processes.

  • Drive the adoption of AI-enabled tools and technologies to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy and enhance team productivity.

  • Ensure process changes are documented appropriately and supported by effective control frameworks.

Stakeholder Management

  • Build strong working relationships across Finance and the wider business to support accurate financial reporting and operational effectiveness.

  • Work collaboratively with Accounts Payable, FP&A, Tax, Treasury, Regulatory Reporting and external auditors to ensure reporting requirements are met.

  • Support audit activities by coordinating information requests and providing timely, accurate responses.

  • Contribute to cross-functional projects requiring accounting, control or process expertise.

What success looks like in the role:

  • Month-end reporting processes are delivered accurately, on time and in line with agreed timetables.

  • The general ledger remains well-controlled, supported and reconciled, with minimal audit findings or control weaknesses.

  • Complex accounting areas, including share-based payments, are supported with accurate analysis, appropriate documentation and clear escalation where technical judgement is required.

  • Practical capex accounting experience is applied to ensure capitalisation and amortisation are accurate, well-supported and appropriately controlled as part of the wider Financial Control remit.

  • Financial control processes become increasingly automated, scalable and efficient as ClearBank grows.

  • AI-enabled tools are successfully adopted to improve productivity, insight and operational effectiveness.

  • Stakeholders receive accurate, timely and reliable financial information that supports decision-making and reporting obligations.

  • The role works effectively with colleagues across Finance and the wider business to deliver high-quality outcomes.

  • Financial Control contributes to a strong control environment while continuously improving efficiency and reducing operational risk.

  • The role demonstrates excellence in both what is delivered and how it is delivered through strong collaboration, ownership, continuous improvement and leadership behaviours.

Skills & Experience (must-have)

  • Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA).

  • Strong financial accounting and financial control experience within a regulated financial services environment.

  • Experience managing month-end close activities, balance sheet reconciliations and general ledger controls.

  • Experience managing the monthly capitalisation and amortisation of intangible assets, including accurate accounting entries, supporting documentation and financial controls.

  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, including experience interpreting and applying accounting standards.

  • Experience supporting complex accounting areas, including preparing analysis and documentation to support technical accounting judgements.

  • Strong understanding of financial controls, governance and audit requirements.

  • Proven ability to identify, lead and implement process improvement initiatives.

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and strong financial analysis capability.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.

  • High attention to detail combined with a pragmatic and solutions-focused mindset.

A little bit more about us! 

ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

  • 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

  • Our enhanced family leave policies

  • Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

  • Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 

Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.  

Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! 

Our commitment to you as a candidate: 

We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time.  

We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully.  

We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon!  

Equal Opportunities

ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. 

ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. 

As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. 

The legal bit

By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes.

title: Founder's Associate Intern
descriptionHtml:

Du entwickelst neue Ideen und Geschäftsansätze mit und bringst sie hands-on in die Umsetzung. Dabei übernimmst du von Anfang an Verantwortung, treibst eigene Projekte voran und sorgst dafür, dass aus Ideen konkrete Ergebnisse werden. Die Energiewende braucht Kapital. Gleichzeitig wächst in Deutschland der Markt für Erneuerbare-Energie-Projekte – doch die passende Finanzierung kommt noch viel zu selten effizient zustande. Was bislang fehlt, ist ein Tech-Layer, der Investoren, Projektentwickler und Banken intelligent miteinander verbindet.

Wir glauben, dass darin enormes Potenzial steckt. Deshalb arbeiten wir aktuell im Stealth Mode an einer neuen Lösung, die genau hier ansetzt. Dafür suchen wir Menschen, die Lust haben, von Anfang an Verantwortung zu übernehmen, eigene Ideen einzubringen und die Entwicklung aktiv mitzugestalten. Was du mitbringst

  • Erste Praktika in Start-ups, Beratung oder Venture Capital.

title: Founding lead Product Designer
descriptionHtml:
Raison is on a mission to provide humans with better skills so they can feel confident and have more opportunities in the AI era. We help companies make sure 100% their teams master AI, directly in the flow of work (Teams, Slack) so that AI knowledge spreads across the organization instead of pooling in a handful of champions.

We are passionate entrepreneurs believing that the ongoing AI revolution should be shared by all employees; and that the future of corporate interactions should not be restricted to private human-machine chats. Raison is capturing what champions create with AI, turning it into shared, governed skills, and propagating them so everyone feels capable and empowered; acting as a powerful lever to accelerate the AI transformation of corporates.

We recently raised €2m from a top French VC + BPI and a selection of high-profile business angels who believe AI mastery is the highest-leverage application of AI inside companies.

Tasks

User Research & Discovery

  • Own field research: contextual inquiry, user interviews, and observation of how teams actually work with AI and where it breaks.
  • Build and maintain a deep understanding of our core users — individual contributors, champions, managers, and corporate buyers — and the context they operate in.
  • Synthesize messy field data into sharp, actionable insight: jobs-to-be-done, adoption blockers, and the conditions under which a skill transfers between people.
  • Establish a continuous discovery habit so research is a foundational reflex, and champion the user's perspective in every product decision.

Product & Experience Design

  • What our experts do by hand today is the spec for what the product must automate tomorrow. Your job is to watch that closely enough to design it.
  • Design the surfaces: the client dashboard execs present to their board, the internal console our experts use to run a dozen live communities at once, and the conversations themselves.
  • Most of our product lives inside someone else's client. You are designing in Teams and Slack, not screens we control — no onboarding, no landing page, no second chance. A four-minute message to an accountant who has never opened Copilot is the hardest design problem we have.
  • Work mostly on enterprise, and partly on higher education, where we also have live deployments. Two audiences, two vocabularies, one product: part of your job is deciding what stays shared and what has to differ, so we build one coherent system rather than two half-products.
  • Work hand-in-hand with our AI product engineers so your field learnings ship as features, then get re-tested at the next pilot.
  • Own the design system: components, tokens, patterns, and the copy that goes with them.

Requirements

  • 4–8 years in product design, UX design, or a hybrid design-research role, ideally on complex, multi-user B2B products.
  • A strong portfolio that shows both craft and thinking: we want to see how you operated, not just what shipped.
  • A skilled researcher who can design a study, run it in the wild, and turn qualitative chaos into clear direction.
  • Experience designing inside environments you don't control - a messaging client, an extension, an embedded product - or a clear appetite for it.
  • Comfortable designing for AI-driven and adaptive experiences, where the interface has to handle uncertainty, personalization, and non-linear workflows.
  • Excellent visual and interaction design skills: typography, spacing, motion, and the small details that build trust.
  • Autonomous and opinionated, but you hold your opinions loosely when the evidence says otherwise.
  • Genuine curiosity about AI and how people actually learn at work.
  • Fluent in French and English, spoken and written. Spanish is a plus.
  • You want the ownership, equity, and career-defining challenge that only comes from being early.
  • Bonus: deeply passionate about something outside of work.

Benefits

  • A founding role with equity and direct influence on company strategy.

  • Competitive salary, benchmarked to the Paris startup ecosystem.

  • Flexibility: remote-friendly with regular in-person collaboration in Paris and an office in Montmartre with a beautiful Sacré-Coeur view.

  • A front-row seat to one of the most important shifts in how humans learn.

  • A small, sharp team that ships fast and trusts each other to figure things out.

  • If you care deeply about making powerful tools feel human and want to shape a product from the very beginning, this is your role. Apply now and help us build the future of learning.

  • Raison is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team.

title: Go-To-Market Associate
descriptionHtml:
About us

Hey there! We're Lleverage, and we're making the Autonomous Back Office actually achievable for businesses. We enable teams to capture, automate, and integrate AI agents into their business, because AI is only useful when it actually fits into daily operations.

We help the most strategic European industries – manufacturing, logistics, and wholesale – automate the messy, manual processes that most tools can’t handle.

We’re a fast-growing, VC-backed scale-up based in Amsterdam, with big ambitions for 2026 and beyond. This is your chance to join early, have real impact, and grow alongside the company. If that sounds something you want to help build, we'd love to have you on board!

About the role

We're looking for an exceptional Go-To-Market Associate who will be the engine of our commercial team. As part of the top 1% of Commercial talents globally, you'll combine systematic prospecting with creative outreach to build relationships with decision-makers who need AI solutions.

This is not a classic sales role. We're looking for a builder with a commercial brain and an enormous drive, someone who combines hustle, strategic creativity, and genuine curiosity about what makes businesses tick.

You might come from a classic sales background, or you might have built your commercial instincts in a completely different arena. What matters far more than your CV is your drive, your entrepreneurial instinct, and the kind of work ethic that makes people wonder how you get so much done.

In a single day you might: map a new industry vertical for outreach opportunities, run a consultative discovery call with a Head of Operations at a manufacturing company, develop a proposal for a new channel, follow up on an active deal in scoping, and draft a business case for entering a completely new market.

You won't have a large team behind you. You will have full autonomy, meaningful equity, direct access to the founding team, and the freedom to experiment with what works.

Why Lleverage?

  • Change the world, literally: 2026 is the year AI works, and Lleverage.ai has the best AI platform (according to industry veterans)

  • Work, learn, have fun: You'll be part of a top-notch commercial team that operates at the highest level of performance

  • Build a unique network: Connect with decision-makers and operational leaders across traditional industries who are eager to implement AI solutions

  • Get autonomy & ownership: Design your own strategies and own your pipeline development

  • Compensation: We pay top of market cash and equity, with compensation tied to the pipeline value you create

Responsibilities

  • Own our top of funnel: which segments we go after, how we reach the COOs and CFOs of manufacturers and distributors, and how many qualified opportunities land in the pipeline every week. That's your number.

  • Sit in on live deals from day one: discovery calls, account plans, proposals and PoC scoping with our delivery team. Within 6 to 12 months you run your first deals yourself.

  • Build the playbook with the GTM lead and CCO: positioning per sector, messaging per persona, pricing experiments, the business cases we win with.

  • Run experiments across the whole funnel: outbound campaigns, events, partnerships with ERP partners and PE firms, LinkedIn content. Measure everything, scale what works.

  • Use AI-native tooling (Clay, lemlist, our own agents) to research, personalise and scale what a team of five used to do by hand, and help us figure out what GTM looks like when AI does the grunt work.

  • Bring what you see in the market to the founding team and product: which use cases, sectors, competitors and prices we should bet on next.


Job specific requirements

  • 1 to 3 years in consulting, investment banking, PE or a fast-growing B2B startup, or you built something yourself.

  • You make things happen without a brief, and can show it with an example and a number.

  • You win trust fast, with a CFO in a boardroom and with an operations manager on a factory floor.

  • You think in funnels and business cases and turn data into a clear recommendation.

  • New sectors, no playbook, channels nobody has tried: that energises you rather than stops you. A no on Monday doesn't define your Tuesday.

  • Genuinely curious about how businesses make money and where they lose it.

  • You want to own revenue within a year and know why.

  • Fluent Dutch and English, German is a big plus

Nice to haves

  • Worked with or for manufacturing, wholesale, logistics or food companies.

  • Hands-on with HubSpot, Clay or lemlist.

  • Understanding of ERP-driven processes (SAP, Business Central, Exact).

  • Sold something before: side business, campus sales, fundraising.

Our Tech Stack

You'll be working with best-in-class tools:

  • CRM: HubSpot for pipeline management

  • Prospecting: AI-powered research and outreach tools like Clay and Lemlist

  • Communication: Multi-channel outreach across email, LinkedIn, and phone

  • Analytics: Data-driven insights to optimize your approach

  • And always exploring what's next

We offer

You are ready for the ride of a lifetime with experienced entrepreneurs and innovators who aim for hyper growth on a global scale. We look for an enormous drive and hands-on mentality. Somebody who can work with us in creating the best AI platform out there!

We offer a good salary, a highly experienced (and very entertaining...) team and considerable share and bonus packages. And last but not least, this is the start of your career to grow to into a commercial lead and to lay the foundation for years to come.

title: Graduate Mechanical Design Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Company

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Hiring now

We are hiring as soon as possible. This role is for someone who has already graduated, or who will complete their degree in time to start with us very soon. We are not able to consider final-year students who graduate in summer 2027 or later, and this is not a graduate scheme with a fixed annual intake.

Role Overview

This is a first full-time engineering role on the NEO-1 satellite. You will design satellite hardware and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised as the design matures, learning from our lead designer and working in a small, multidisciplinary team. You will take ownership of real parts early, translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, such as brackets, panels, component mounts, thermal-control hardware and cable and harness routing, with guidance from the lead designer.

  • Work in the satellite's large 3D CAD assembly alongside the wider design team, learning how to keep interfaces, configurations and revisions in step as several designers work in the same model.

  • Support assembly configuration, PLM data (3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX') or similar), bills of materials and engineering change control (ECO/ECR/ECN), so that models, drawings and interfaces stay consistent as changes are released.

  • Run interference and clash checks and help maintain the digital mock-up, working with each subsystem owner to allocate space and resolve conflicts.

  • Produce dimensioned, manufacturing-ready drawings using GD&T, with review from senior engineers.

  • Support design reviews (PDR and CDR) and qualification, working with structural and thermal engineers.

  • Work with manufacturers and suppliers to make designs easier to build, and to balance cost, mass and reliability.

  • Support prototype builds, integration and environmental test campaigns, iterating designs based on results.

  • Collaborate with electrical, software, systems and thermal engineers to integrate mechanical components into the satellite platform.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in mechanical, aerospace or a related engineering discipline, completed or completing very soon.

  • Hands-on 3D CAD skills from university projects, a placement or an internship (SolidWorks preferred; CATIA, NX or Creo also considered).

  • Working knowledge of GD&T and experience producing engineering drawings, including from coursework or a team project.

  • Solid grounding in mechanical design principles, materials and thermal management, with a working understanding of structural mechanics.

  • Evidence of designing, building and testing something real, such as a placement project, Formula Student, a UAV, or a rocketry or satellite team, including troubleshooting and iteration.

  • Clear communicator who is comfortable explaining and defending design decisions, and open to feedback and challenge in a fast-moving team.

Preferred Experience

  • A placement, internship or year in industry in aerospace, space, motorsport or another high-reliability field.

  • Experience of several people working in one CAD assembly, for example in a Formula Student or university team, including how files and revisions were controlled.

  • Exposure to PLM or PDM systems (for example 3DEXPERIENCE ('3DX'), Windchill, Teamcenter, ENOVIA or SolidWorks PDM) or to formal engineering change processes (ECO/ECR/ECN).

  • Experience of design reviews, documented requirements and standards.

  • Satellite, CubeSat or rocketry project experience, including hardware that has launched.

  • Basic FEA familiarity and exposure to manufacturing processes.

Why NewOrbit Space?

  • Pioneering space technology - Your work on our RF gridded ion thrusters and VLEO satellite platform will redefine satellite operations and challenge traditional LEO.

  • Ownership and impact - You'll have a level of ownership that's rare in the space industry, and you'll take part in the full lifecycle of satellite technology.

  • Equity and competitive salary - Alongside a competitive salary you receive a company ownership stake, so you share in the technology you help build and in our collective success.

  • Comprehensive benefits - Private health insurance with dental and optical cover, and annual health check-ups.

  • Hybrid working - One dedicated remote day per week.

  • Visa sponsorship and relocation support - We sponsor visas and provide relocation support for candidates moving to join us.

title: Graduate Partnership Executive
descriptionHtml:
About us

Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Lululemon and many more use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform - and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.

The Graduate Opportunity at Fospha

Joining Fospha’s graduate programme means stepping into a fast-paced environment where you’ll gain real responsibility and exposure from day one. In Partnerships, graduates work directly with some of the world’s biggest digital platforms - like TikTok, Meta, and Snapchat - playing a key role in strengthening relationships, enabling joint initiatives, and driving partner success.

  • Hands-on exposure to our Partnerships: Working directly with the platforms such as Tiktok, Meta and Snap, you will build commercial acumen, develop strategic communication skills, and gain a deep understanding of how the digital advertising ecosystem works.
  • Cross-Functional Exposure: With support, cross-functional collaboration, and the opportunity to make a visible impact early on, it’s the ideal launchpad for ambitious graduates looking to break into the world of ad tech and strategic partnerships.
  • Comprehensive Training: In addition to the extensive on-the-job learning opportunities, you'll receive a broad and blended in-person training curriculum covering essential topics such as Business Storytelling, Relationship Building, Market Research & Product and Financial Management.

The Role:

As a Partnerships Executive, you'll join a high-impact team focused on enabling, scaling, and deepening Fospha’s relationships with the platforms that power digital marketing.

This is a graduate-level role designed to develop future leaders. You’ll be hands-on with major ad platforms, supporting both strategic execution and day-to-day coordination. You’ll also work closely with internal teams - especially Marketing, Product and our Customer Teams - to make sure our partners have what they need to help customers grow.

Key responsibilities:

  • Supporting our partner managers in coordinating with Google, Meta, TikTok, Snap and others

What are we looking for?

We hire for potential – you don’t need a technical degree or marketing background. You should apply if you:

  • Are an excellent communicator – written, verbal, and visual

  • Are curious about how marketing, measurement and partnerships work
  • Can handle multiple workstreams and work well under light-touch supervision
  • Thrive in fast-moving, high-growth environments
  • Want to make a real commercial impact from day one

Bonus Points For:

  • Experience with TikTok Ads, Meta, or other digital marketing tools
  • Familiarity with platforms like Notion, HubSpot, Google Sheets
  • Any internship or part-time experience in partnerships, sales, marketing or client-facing roles
  • Like shopping and are a customer of retail brands

Our Values and Principles

You will be able to demonstrate examples of our core principles:

  • Seek inclusion & diversity: We create an environment where everyone feels welcome, and people are encouraged to speak and be heard
  • Work Hard, Work Well, Work Together: We take responsibility for making things happen, independently and together; we help colleagues in need and close loops, making sure our work is complete and has lasting impact
  • Grow: We are proactive, curious and unafraid of failure
  • Customer at the heart: We care about the customer, feel their pain and love building product that solves their biggest problems
  • Candour with caring: We deliver candid feedback with kindness and receive it with gratitude

What we can offer you

  • A workplace pension, through Royal London, with Fospha matching your contributions up to 3%
  • A £1,000/year flexible benefits allowance to put towards private medical insurance, dental cover, a health cash plan, gym membership, extra holiday, or a pension top-up - whatever suits you!
  • Access to Wellhub, giving you one membership across gyms, boutique studios, and wellbeing apps

The Process

title: Graduate Silicon Architect 2027
descriptionHtml:
Location: Bristol, UK
Salary: £45,000 per annum 
Start date: September 2027
Application deadline: Midnight, 29th November 2026 
We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.

The Graduate Programme at Graphcore

Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.

What you’ll work on 

Put your understanding of computer architecture to work on the choices that shape Graphcore’s next generation of AI hardware. 

As a Graduate Silicon Architect, you’ll help specify, model and evaluate complex system-on-chip (SoC) subsystems, with guidance from experienced architects. You’ll explore how product requirements translate into technical options, design trade-offs and validation plans. 

Your work will likely include some of: taking responsibility for the architecture of a chip subsystem or function, modelling architectural features, assessing third-party intellectual property (IP) and supporting silicon bring-up. Working across design, verification, hardware and software teams, you’ll help gather the performance evidence that supports architecture decisions. 

Your team and support 

The Silicon Architecture team sits within the Silicon group. We stand for practical ambition: clear thinking, careful engineering and curiosity that improves real systems. 

You’ll work with mentors and experienced architects through design reviews, modelling, simulation, documentation and discussions with neighbouring teams. You’ll take ownership of defined tasks that grow in scope as you develop your skills. 

Simulations, performance data and design constraints help guide our decisions. You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. Take responsibility for your work and speak up when something needs testing, explaining or support. 

How you’ll learn and grow 

During the two-year programme, you’ll develop your architecture skills through hands-on architectural design + integration, modelling and evaluation of AI acceleration hardware, supported by mentors. 

Exploring technical options and running simulations will help you understand how architecture choices affect system behaviour. You’ll learn how to compare trade-offs, document findings and use performance evidence to support a decision. 

Design reviews and work across engineering teams will help you connect specifications to implementation and validation. Supporting silicon bring-up will give you experience of how architectural ideas are checked on real hardware, while tasks that grow in scope will build your technical judgement and confidence. 

What we’re looking for 

  • A degree, or expected degree, in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science or a related field 
  • An understanding of computer architecture or digital systems, with an interest in SoC design, AI hardware or high-performance computing 
  • Programming experience in Python, Rust, C++ or a similar language 
  • Analytical problem-solving skills and clear written and verbal communication, including documenting findings and explaining technical ideas 

You can demonstrate these skills through coursework, a dissertation, personal or team projects, research, or other relevant experience. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned. 

Exposure to register-transfer level (RTL) design, modelling, simulation, PCIe, Ethernet or DDR would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements. 

Benefits

  • Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility
  • Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension
  • Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success
  • Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day
  • Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones
  • Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice
  • Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover
  • Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn

We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.

We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.

Sponsorship

Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.

Introduction to Graphcore

At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.

How to apply and what to expect 

To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.

Ready to put your learning into practice? Start your career in a permanent SoC Architecture Engineer role, with two years of hands-on learning through the Graphcore Graduate Programme. Apply now and help shape what comes next.

descriptionHtml:

We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line

Being a GRC Engineer at incident.io means turning compliance from spreadsheets and screenshots into something that just runs, so “can you prove it?” gets answered before anyone asks.

What that looks like day to day

As a GRC Engineer at incident.io, you own how we prove we’re doing the right thing: our compliance programme, our customer security questionnaires, and the evidence behind both. One day you’re building an AI workflow that drafts questionnaire answers, the next you’re pushing our ISO 27001 work forward, the next you’re telling the product team what makes GRC painful.

Our GRC programme is young, and Slack is our system of record. You’ll make it scale, using AI-powered tooling and workflows to take the toil out of audits, evidence collection and customer questions.

Right now, that means:

  • ISO 27001. It’s in progress, and you’ll help raise the bar and get us over the line.

  • ISO 42001. We build AI products, so we want to manage AI responsibly. In your first two quarters or so, you’ll run a gap assessment against the standard.

  • Dogfooding. We use incident.io for our own security work, and you’ll drive product improvements that make GRC less painful for our customers too.

You’ll work closely with the wider security team, engineering, legal and product.

Who you are

  • You’ve run or contributed to a real compliance programme, ideally ISO 27001, and you know what it takes to get through an audit.

  • You’d rather automate evidence collection than chase people for screenshots.

  • You write code (Python, Go or similar) or build workflows, and you’re excited about using AI and agents to remove toil.

  • You can answer customer security questionnaires quickly, accurately and in plain English.

  • You can explain a control to an engineer and a risk to an executive, and both come away knowing what to do next.

  • You care about the product, and you’ll tell us what’s missing from our own GRC tooling.

  • You’re comfortable with high autonomy. Nobody’s going to hand you a detailed spec, you’re trusted to figure out what needs doing and just do it.

  • Bonus points for ISO 42001 or AI governance experience, SOC 2, GDPR, or time in a fast-growing SaaS company.

Supporting you

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

  • Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover - we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

  • Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

  • First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

  • Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

  • Meaningful equity. We’re rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

  • Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We’re all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

  • Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we’re doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

  • Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

title: GTM Engineer - Sales Automation and Analytics Management
descriptionHtml:
As a GTM Engineer - Sales Automation and Analytics Management (m/w/d), you will make our sales engine more productive across all PERGOLUX markets globally: more revenue per worked sales hour, less leakage between lead and order, and a lower cost per sale. Reporting to the Head of Sales Operations, you will own two pillars of work, insight and planning on one side, orchestration and automation on the other, partnering daily with Sales Leads in every market, the Data team, Marketing, Customer Service and our Tier 1 partner. This is a builder-operator role: the Data team owns the data foundation, and you use it to find what is holding sales back, then fix it with a mix of planning, incentives, process automation and AI.

PERGOLUX designs and sells premium, Scandinavian-inspired outdoor living products, from aluminium pergolas to awnings and garden furniture, directly to consumers. We are a company that has grown consistently across Europe and beyond, with around 300 employees, 9-figure revenue and operations across eight markets.

What You'll Do

- Analyse the full funnel (lead, contact, qualification, draft order, order) by market, tier, channel and rep, mine call, chat and CRM activity for conversion patterns, and run a monthly insight cycle of three to five prioritised findings, each with an owner, an action and a measured result.

- Own the global capacity model for Tier 1, Tier 2, showroom and Customer Service fallback coverage, run the monthly refresh and seasonal peak plan, and flag hiring, reallocation or BPO volume changes early while tracking planned versus actual coverage with Sales Leads and Finance.

- Run the monthly and quarterly bonus calculations for Sales Leads, Tier 2 reps and the Tier 1 partner payout, test and model each scheme before changes go live, and automate the calculation and reporting so payouts need checks rather than manual builds.

- Own revenue per worked hour as the core productivity KPI, from definition and baseline to targets and monthly reporting by market and tier, and lead initiatives that move its drivers of productive time, conversion and order value.

- Orchestrate sales activity through task queues, lead prioritisation, follow-up cadences and reactivation, map and automate our sales processes in HubSpot (with Aircall, Shopify and messaging integrations), and run AI pilots across the funnel with clear success metrics and a running business case per use case.

What You'll Bring

- Proven experience in sales operations, revenue operations or GTM engineering, turning sales, call and order data into decisions and measurable KPI movement.

- Strong analytical skills across the full funnel, with the ability to write clear requirements for a data team and validate what they ship.

- Hands-on experience building HubSpot workflows and integrations with tools such as Aircall, Shopify and messaging platforms, within agreed data governance.

- A builder-operator mindset: you design capacity models, incentive schemes and process automation, then operate and iterate on them rather than only reporting.

- Practical experience deploying AI use cases across a sales funnel (speed-to-lead, qualification, summaries, next-best-action, follow-up drafting) is a strong plus.

💼 Compensation — Attractive, competitive salary · Company pension plan · Capped overtime, fully paid, with no endless unpaid crunch · 20% commission on base salary plus a maximum 30% additional bonus for exceeding targets

🚀 Growth and Career Development — You will take real ownership from the start with direct impact on key revenue outcomes, work alongside an international, collaborative team across Europe, and have a fast-track path to grow into senior leadership as PERGOLUX scales.

⏰ Time Off and Flexibility — Up to 30 vacation days, starting at 27 · One week per year remote workation in the EU/UK
